newsitem.title: USA: CytoTherapeutics gets money for testing.
newsitem.headline: CytoTherapeutics gets money for testing.

text.p: CytoTherapeutics Inc said Tuesday it had received $3 million as a milestone payment from Astra Ab of Sweden to further test a device designed to control pain in a patient.
The company said the money would help finance Phase II of a clinical trial program for an Analgesic Cell Therapy Implantable Device, or ACTID, which is a cell-containing, pain-control implant.
The payment brings to more than $23 million the amount of funding it has received from Astra under a collaborative agreement, it said.
Astra is to have the exclusive worldwide right to market products covered by the agreement.
CytoTherapeutics said it is entitled to a royalty on worldwide net sales of ACTID, which the company is expected to manufacture and supply to Astra.
Astra is a pharmaceutical company focused on developing treatments for respiratory, gastrointestinal and cardiovascular diseases and pain control.
CytoTherapeutics develops cell therapy systems designed to deliver therapeutic substances to the central nervous system.
